1. Introduction 
This document provides information about fleet card processing with the BUYPASS® platform 
(BUYPASS). 
The following sections of the latest release of BUYPASS Platform Petroleum Processing 
Specifications will be updated to include Voyager Chip processing requirements: 
• 10, Voyager Fleet Card Processing 
• 10.2, EMV Processing Requirements 
• 10.3, Card Formats 
• Appendix I, Voyager Chip-Specific POS Prompt Codes 
• Appendix J, Voyager Terminal Capabilities (9F33) 
• Appendix K, Voyager Additional Terminal Capabilities (9F40) 
• Appendix L, Voyager Terminal Action Codes 
The scope of the information contained in this document is described in the chapter descriptions 
listed below. 
The audiences of this document include decision makers evaluating BUYPASS services and the 
programmers and analysts who implement and support these services. 
This document contains the following chapters and appendices: 
1.  Introduction.  This chapter lists and describes each chapter and appendix in this document. 
2.  Automated Fuel Pump Processing Overview.  This chapter discusses configuration 
options, configuration requirements, and controller system activities for automated fuel pump 
(AFP) processing. 
3.  Transaction Requirements.  This chapter discusses point-of-sale (POS) Authorization 
Only, POS Purchase/Capture, customer-activated terminal (CAT) Authorization Only, CAT 
Purchase/Capture, POS Return/Refund, POS Reversal/Void, POS Time-out Reversal, and CAT 
Time-out Reversal transaction requirements. 
4.  Receipt Requirements.  This chapter discusses the information that is printed on fleet card 
receipts. 
5.  Fleet One Fleet Card Processing.  This chapter discusses processing requirements, card 
layout, and embossing standards for Fleet One fleet cards. 
6.  Fuelman™/Fleetwide Fleet Card Processing.  This chapter discusses processing 
requirements, card layout, and embossing standards for Fuelman/Fleetwide fleet cards. 
7.  MasterCard® Fleet Card Processing.  This chapter discusses processing requirements, 
card layout, and embossing standards for MasterCard fleet cards. 
8.  Visa® Fleet Card Processing.  This chapter discusses processing requirements, card 
layout, and embossing standards for Visa fleet cards. 
9.  Voyager℠ Fleet Card Processing.  This chapter discusses processing requirements, card 
layout, and embossing standards for Voyager fleet cards.

2. Automated Fuel Pump Processing Overview 
This chapter discusses the following automated fuel pump (AFP) processing topics: 
• Configuration options 
• Configuration requirements 
• Controller system activities 
 Debit cards 
 Stored value cards 
The BUYPASS automated fuel pump (AFP) interface provides a controller-based AFP system 
with the ability to communicate with BUYPASS.  This ability enables the AFP interface to 
request authorizations for and draft capture of credit card, debit card, fleet card, stored value 
card, and oil company card purchases. 
The following information is determined at the controller of the AFP system: 
• Card type 
• Intended purchase amount or authorization amount 
• Indication whether payment request is from a customer-activated device 
• Any other required input from the purchaser or station attendant

2.2. Configuration Requirements 
The following off-line transaction parameters should be configurable: 
• Dollar amount 
• Number of transactions 
• Total off-line dollar amount 
If transactions go into off-line mode, the numbers for controller-generated receipts must start 
with LA0001 and be incremented by 1 for each transaction. 
A transaction can be submitted up to three times or reformatted and resubmitted one more time 
after a device reestablishes connectivity.  If, after these attempts, the transaction is not captured 
at BUYPASS, log that transaction in the Daily Exception Log.  The Daily Exception Log attempts 
to retransmit its information one more time before the end-of-day settlement.  That log should 
print at the end of the day, along with the Totals Report. 
A transaction that has been declined by BUYPASS cannot be resubmitted. 
Note: Transaction resubmission is subject to the message format rules regarding time-out 
reversals.

2.3. Controller System Activities 
This section describes specific controller system activities related to the following card types: 
• Debit cards 
• Credit cards 
• Stored value cards 
2.3.1. Debit Cards 
When processing a debit card completion, the transaction can only be processed one time by 
BUYPASS and debit networks.  This transaction cannot be reversed or processed again by the 
device. 
In the event that the device sends a debit card completion to BUYPASS and does not receive a 
response, the device must resend the request on the next connection attempt or within 15 
minutes after the transaction took place, whichever occurs first.  Once BUYPASS receives the 
completion request, a corresponding response code will be sent back to the device.  If the 
transaction is declined with a response code value of 1 and a value of 24 returned in position 
nos. 15 and 16 of the device decline message, the device should consider the transaction as 
already captured at BUYPASS.  The device should then reflect the transaction as approved and 
update the device totals. 
Any response from BUYPASS to a debit card completion should end attempts to retry the debit 
card completion, regardless of whether it was approved or declined. 
For Message Format Version Identifier ATL100 and higher, the Approved Amount in an 
approved Authorization Only response (Response Code = 0) in a debit card transaction can 
differ from the requested amount. 
Note: Message Format Version Identifier ATL100 does not support partial approvals for debit 
financial transactions. 
For Message Format Version Identifier ATL101 and higher, the Approved Amount in an 
approved Partial Approval response (Response Code = F) in a debit card transaction is different 
from the requested amount. 
2.3.2. Credit Cards 
For petroleum credit card processing, the CAT Purchase/Completion transaction must be 
transmitted from the device no later than 55 minutes after its creation by the controller.

2.3.3. Stored Value Cards 
For Message Format Version Identifier ATL100 and higher, the Approved Amount in an 
approved Authorization Only response (Response Code = 0) in a stored value card transaction 
can differ from the requested amount.  An example would be when the requested amount 
exceeds the current balance on the stored value card. 
For Message Format Version Identifier ATL101 and higher, the Approved Amount in a Partial 
Approval response (Response Code = F) in a stored value card transaction is different from the 
requested amount. 
To accommodate either of these situations, the device needs to be set to do the following: 
• Pump the Approved Amount—not the requested amount 
• Process the response for the amount approved 
• On non-CAT transactions, handle the remaining balance as a split tender transaction

3. Transaction Requirements 
This chapter describes the following transactions: 
• POS Authorization Only Transaction 
• POS Purchase/Capture Transaction 
• Customer-activated Terminal (CAT) Authorization Only Transaction 
 Address Verification Service Feature 
• Customer-activated Terminal (CAT) Purchase/Capture Transaction 
• POS Return/Refund Transaction 
• POS Reversal/Void Transaction 
• POS Time-out Reversal Transaction

Each transaction’s description contains the following information: 
• Purpose of the transaction 
• Other involved transactions, if any 
• What action initiates the transaction 
• What action completes the transaction 
• Whether the payment method can be by debit, credit, fleet, stored value, or proprietary card 
• Whether a receipt is printed 
• Related transaction processing 
• Related transaction flow 
• Whether address verification is used

3.1. POS Authorization Only Transaction 
A POS Authorization Only transaction originates at a POS device.  This transaction verifies 
cardholder account fund availability for the specific dollar amount of the purchase, and 
authorizes the purchase for that specific dollar amount. 
This transaction is not dependent upon any other transaction.  
This transaction is initiated after all data entry and data validation is completed locally.  The 
POS device transmits a POS Authorization Only request to BUYPASS and waits for a valid 
response. 
A POS Authorization Only transaction is used when a Prepay transaction is initiated from the 
indoor POS device and authorizes a pump to dispense fuel for a specific amount.  A Prepay 
transaction uses a POS Capture transaction to complete the transaction once fueling is finished.  
Both of these transactions are initiated from the indoor POS device. 
This transaction is completed when a valid response is received from BUYPASS. 
Valid payment methods for a POS Authorization Only transaction are:  debit, credit, fleet, stored 
value, or proprietary card. 
Valid payment methods for a Prepay transaction are:  credit, fleet or proprietary cards. 
No receipt is required for this transaction. 
This transaction does not use address verification.

3.2. POS Purchase/Capture Transaction 
A POS Purchase/Capture transaction originates at a POS device.  It accomplishes any one of 
the four following transaction activities: 
• Inside purchase 
An inside purchase is completed when a cardholder authorizes a POS device to transmit 
captured cardholder and product information (for the inside purchase) to BUYPASS where 
verification, authorization, and capture processes occur. 
This activity is not dependent upon any other transaction. 
• Capture of Prepay 
A Prepay transaction is completed when fuel pumping is finished, and a POS Capture 
transaction is initiated. A sale is actually posted to a cardholder’s account during a POS 
Completion transaction. 
• Capture of POS authorization only 
The capture of POS authorization only information is completed when a POS device 
transmits cardholder authorization and purchased product information from a previous 
Authorization Only transaction to BUYPASS. 
This activity is dependent upon an Authorization Only transaction. 
• Forced/Off-line purchase 
A forced/off-line purchase is completed when the POS device captures the cardholder and 
purchased product information and then uses an authorization code from a system other 
than BUYPASS to authorize the purchase.  The POS device then transmits this information 
to BUYPASS where verification and capture processes occur. 
This activity is not dependent upon any other transaction. 
This transaction is initiated when a POS device transmits a POS Purchase/Capture request to 
BUYPASS and waits for a valid response. 
This transaction is completed when a valid POS Purchase/Capture Response is received from 
BUYPASS. 
Valid payment methods for an inside purchase are:  debit, credit, fleet, stored value, EBT, or 
proprietary cards. 
Valid payment methods for a Prepay transaction are:  credit, fleet or proprietary cards. 
Valid payment methods for a capture of POS Authorization only are:  credit, fleet, or proprietary 
cards. 
Valid payment methods for a forced/off-line purchase transaction are:  credit, fleet, and 
proprietary cards. 
A receipt is printed for the POS Authorization Only transaction for the specific dollar amount.  If 
the amount of the actual purchase is different from the amount printed on the POS Authorization 
Only receipt, another receipt is printed for the POS Capture transaction for the actual dollar 
amount of the purchase.

3.3. Customer-Activated Terminal Authorization Only 
Transaction 
A CAT Authorization Only transaction originates at a CAT.  This transaction verifies cardholder 
account fund availability, and secures sufficient cardholder account funds for a purchase using a 
CAT. 
This transaction is not dependent upon any other transaction. 
This transaction is initiated when a cardholder swipes a card through a card reader activating 
the CAT.  The CAT transmits the transaction containing a preset dollar amount (configurable at 
the CAT by card type) to BUYPASS and waits for a valid response. 
This transaction is completed when a valid response is received from BUYPASS. 
Note: Please refer to the appropriate message format specifications for processing information 
about partial approvals of Authorization Only transaction requests. 
Valid payment methods are:  debit, credit, fleet, stored value, or proprietary card. 
A receipt can be printed after fuel has been dispensed if the cardholder selects this option. 
Address verification is an optional feature for this transaction. 
Note: The Address Verification Service (AVS) feature must be configurable by card type for 
CAT transactions at the device.  See section 3.3.1, "Address Verification Service 
Feature," for additional information.

3.3.1. Address Verification Service Feature 
Note: Contact your BUYPASS representative for additional fee information involving the use of 
AVS. 
For outside transactions, AVS enables a petroleum merchant to confirm the identity of a 
cardholder in order to prevent fraudulent use of a card. 
For outside transactions, AVS is required at the CAT for CAT Authorization Only transactions.  
The device must prompt for the cardholder’s billing address zip code.  If the financial portion of 
the transaction is approved, and the zip code validation is negative, the customer must be sent 
inside to complete the transaction.  The card must be presented for payment.  The merchant 
decides how to complete the transaction.  The device takes no action.  The AVS feature must 
be configurable by card type at the controller for CAT Authorization Only transactions. 
This transaction is initiated when a cardholder swipes a card through a card reader activating 
the CAT. 
The device display then prompts for entry of the cardholder's 5- or 9-digit zip code (Format:  
##### or #########) on the device's keypad.  An Authorization Only transaction is sent 
containing a set dollar amount, configurable at the controller by card type, and the AVS zip 
code.  The transaction is completed according to the Authorization Response Code and the 
AVS response from the card issuer in the transaction response.  To activate the pump, the 
Authorization Response must be an approval for both the Authorization Only amount and a 
positive response in the AVS zip code.  Any negative response or no response about the AVS 
zip code cancels the transaction and directs the customer inside to complete the sale as a POS 
Purchase/Capture transaction.  A receipt is printed after fuel has been dispensed if the 
cardholder selects this option. 
Valid credit card payment methods can be: 
• American Express® 
• MasterCard 
• Discover® Network 
• Visa

3.4. Customer-Activated Terminal Purchase/Capture 
Transaction 
A CAT Purchase/Capture transaction completes a fuel purchase transaction, by forwarding the 
final total purchase amount to BUYPASS. 
This transaction is dependent upon the CAT Authorization Only transaction, which is initiated 
when the cardholder swipes a card through a card reader activating the CAT.  The final total 
purchase amount cannot exceed the authorized amount in the completed CAT Authorization 
Only transaction. 
The CAT Purchase/Capture transaction is initiated when the pump nozzle is returned to the 
pump after fuel dispensing is complete, and the final total purchase amount is calculated. 
This transaction is completed when the final total purchase amount is transmitted to BUYPASS 
in one of the following ways: 
• either while the current communications session is still established; or 
• in a subsequent communications session when the device sends the next transaction 
request to BUYPASS. 
Note: Refer to section 2.3, “Controller System Activities,” for transaction storage and 
transmission timeframe requirements. 
Valid payment methods are:  debit, credit, fleet, stored value, or proprietary card. 
A receipt can be printed after fuel has been dispensed if the cardholder selects this option. 
This transaction does not use address verification.

3.5. POS Return/Refund Transaction 
The purpose of a POS Return/Refund transaction is to return/refund to the cardholder a portion 
or all of a previously processed Purchase transaction. 
No other transactions are involved in a POS Return/Refund transaction. 
A POS Return/Refund transaction is always initiated when a cardholder returns an item that was 
purchased on a previous business day. 
A POS Return/Refund transaction is completed when a valid response is received from 
BUYPASS. 
Valid payment methods are:  all debit, all credit, some fleet, all stored value, or all proprietary 
cards. 
A receipt must be printed. 
Address verification is not used with a POS Return/Refund transaction.

3.6. POS Reversal/Void Transaction 
The purpose of a POS Reversal/Void transaction is to cancel a previously approved transaction 
for a purchase that was made during the current business day.  This transaction is typically 
used when an error is made and not discovered until after a receipt has been printed for the 
customer. 
This transaction depends on a prior POS Purchase Capture transaction. 
A POS Reversal/Void transaction is initiated when an error is discovered or a cardholder returns 
an item that was purchased during the current business day. 
To implement a POS Reversal/Void transaction, a POS device should reconstruct exactly the 
previously approved transaction without requiring the operator to reenter all information.  If this 
is not possible, then, at a minimum, the following information must be entered in order for the 
POS Reversal/Void transaction to process: 
• Account Number 
• Sequence Number 
• Exact dollars-and-cents amount 
• Approval Code from the previously approved transaction 
A POS Reversal/Void transaction is completed when a valid response is received from 
BUYPASS.  If the POS Reversal/Void transaction is declined, then a POS Return/Refund 
transaction needs to be performed. 
A receipt is printed. 
Address verification is not used with a POS Reversal/Void transaction.

4. Receipt Requirements 
This chapter discusses the following information that must print on fleet card receipts: 
• Merchant information 
• BUYPASS Platform Merchant Number 
• Card Type ID 
• Account Number 
 Truncation requirements 
 Manual entry requirements 
• Expiration Date 
• Transaction Date 
• Transaction Time 
• Sequence Number 
• Product information 
• Vehicle Number 
• Odometer Reading 
• Approved/Declined message 
• Signature Line 
Note: Please refer to the corresponding message format specifications for receipt information 
about other card types.

9.2.1.1. Technology Selection 
Voyager Cards do not follow the ISO7813 standards for Track data encoding, and as a result, 
the service code on Voyager Cards is not currently positioned where terminals expect to find 
them.  This has impacts to terminal logic in determining whether or not a card is chip capable.  
In the EMV world, terminals will check for the Service Code in the track data in the position 
immediately following the expiration date.  When an EMV card is swiped first, and the first 
position of the Service Code is a ‘2’ or a ‘6’, the terminal will prompt the cardholder to insert their 
card to try and force the use of chip before the magstripe is used. 
 
Terminals supporting Voyager Cards for EMV must be able to check for the service code in 
position 31 of the track2 data or position 58 of the track1 data.  If a Voyager card is swiped first, 
terminals must check position 31 (Track2) or position 58 (track1) to determine if the service 
code begins with a ‘2’ or ‘6’.  If this position does start with a ‘2’ or ‘6’ then the terminal must 
request the cardholder to insert their card into the chip reader. 
 
In addition, a new value will be included in both Track1 and Track 2 for ‘Truck Class’ beginning 
in Position 63 and 36 respectively.  Please see Voyager EMV terminal Specifications v1.5 for 
more details.

9.2.1.4. Prompting 
When chip technology is used, the payment will be processed using a unique Voyager 
Application Identifier (AID) which will leverage the Third Party Data tag (Tag 9F6E). Depending 
on the type of card used, prompting at the terminal will vary based on the Voyager Restriction 
and Prompt Code found on the chip. However, the payment application and payment 
configuration are identical for all types of cards. The Third Party Data tag carries specific 
product information to be used by the terminal in processing prompts as part of the transactions 
and the pre-authorization. 
Enhanced Fleet prompting is a mechanism that provides greater flexibility to Voyager on 
capturing Level 3 type data at terminals where Voyager Fleet EMV cards are accepted.  It 
replaces the current process of using Product and Restriction codes located in the discretionary 
data of both track1 and track2 on the magstripe.  The Enhanced Fleet Prompting simplifies the 
terminal by removing the need to generate prompting logic around these restriction and product 
codes.  Instead, the terminal will read required prompt messages directly from the Voyager Fleet 
card itself.  This allows Voyager the flexibility to tailor prompts specifically for their fleet 
customer’s needs.   
The terminal must make the following validations to determine if the card product supports  
Enhanced Fleet Processing: 
• Third Party Data (9F6E) is present in the FCI of the Voyager Fleet ADF 
• Terminals supporting Voyager EMV Fleet cards must use the Third Party Data 
(Tag 9F6E) to determine if card/application supports Enhanced Fleet 
Prompting 
• A value of ‘0003’ or ‘8003’ in the Unique Identifier of the Third Party Data 
(9F6E) indicates that Enhanced Fleet Prompting is supported by the card 
product. 
• Unique Identifiers other than ‘0003’ or ‘8003’ is not to be considered as a 
Voyager Fleet product 
• The Product Identifier within the Proprietary Data component of the Third Party 
Data must be set to ‘0001’ to indicate Enhanced Fleet Support.   Any other 
value indicates non-fleet product. 
 
For Voyager cards that are setup where the Product Type Code does not indicate support of the 
Prompt Script File, the terminal must then prompt for the terminal-defined prompts specified in bit 
4-1 of the Product Type Code.  These prompts are limited to Odometer (bit 4), Driver Number (bit 
3), Vehicle Number (bit 2) and ID Number (bit 1).  These fields must be prompted in the order of 
the highest order bit defined (bit 4, then bit 3, etc.). 
 
For Voyager cards that are setup where the Product Type Code does indicate support of the 
Prompt Script File, the terminal must read said file and prompt as indicated.  See ‘Appendix I, 
“Voyager Chip-Specific POS Prompt Codes.’ for specifics on Enhanced prompts.

Voyager Chip cards are accepted at both Unattended and Attended terminals: 
Unattended terminals: 
• Support of ‘No CVM Required’ is mandatory 
• Support of online enciphered PIN is mandatory 
• Support of offline PIN is not allowed 
• Support of signature is not allowed

• Support of offline PIN is not allowed 
• Support of signature is mandatory 
9.2.2.4. Offline Card Authentication Methods 
Voyager requirements related to the support of offline Card Authentication Methods (CAM) are: 
• An offline capable terminal must support both DDA and CDA (SDA is optional) 
• An online-only terminal may support no offline CAM 
• When CDA is supported, CDA must be implemented according to EMV 4.2 or later versions.  
The terminal must use the CDA EMV-defined Mode n°1 defined in EMV 4.3 - Book 2 that 
consists in: 
o Request CDA on 1st GENERATE AC command on ARQC, and 
o Request CDA on 2nd GENERATE AC on TC after approved online authorization. 
• When CDA is supported, the terminal should verify before Terminal Action Analysis that it 
contains the Certification Authority Public Key identified by the card.  Terminals that can 
perform RSA certificate verification quickly are recommended to retrieve the Issuer public 
key and ICC public key prior Terminal Action Analysis. 
• When offline CAM is supported, the terminal must be capable to support at least two 
Voyager Certification Authority Public Keys for the Voyager RID.  (EMV mandates to support 
at least 6 Certification Authority Public Keys per RID) 
• When offline CAM is supported, the terminal must be capable to support RSA key length of 
248 bytes and RSA key exponent equal to either 3 or (216 + 1) 
• The terminal must be capable to check the integrity of the Certification Authority Public 
Keys.

10.1.6. Expiration Date 
The device must perform an expiration date validation on all WEX fleet card transactions.  The 
card’s Expiration Date is suppressed on the cardholder receipt. 
10.1.7. Check Digit Calculation 
Mod 10 Check Digit Calculation is performed using positions 7–12 of the Account Number, 
applying the check digit to position 13 of the Account Number.   
10.1.8. Vehicle Card Number (Purchase Device Sequence 
Number) 
The Vehicle Card Number is a 5-digit number.  It is encoded in the Track 2 data and embossed 
on the front of the card under the label “Vehicle Card No.”  Newer WEX cards will show the label 
“Purchase Dev Seq.” 
Vehicle Card Number prompting is required only for manual entry transactions. 
The Vehicle Card Number prints on both swiped and manually entered transactions, even 
though no prompting is involved for swiped transactions. 
Please refer to Appendix A, “Petroleum Industry Device Prompt Requirements,” for a summary 
of card prompting requirements and Appendix D, “WEX-Specific POS Prompt Codes.” 
10.1.9. Purchase Restriction Code 
In offline processing mode, the device performs a purchase restriction check against Field 7 of 
the Track 2 data. 
Please refer to section 10.2, “Card Layout,” for a description of Purchase Restriction Code 
values. 
Please refer to Appendix B, “Valid Payment Systems Product Codes,” for additional 
information. 
Note: A unique Product Code must be sent for each type of fuel purchase.

10.1.10. Authorization Amount 
For all WEX fleet card automated fuel pump (AFP) transactions, the WEX host returns an 
approved maximum dollar amount in the Authorization Response that is used to authorize the 
pump.  This amount may differ from the amount in the original Authorization Request 
transmitted by the device.  If the approved maximum dollar amount is more than the AFP pump 
limit, the pump limit may take precedence.  If the approved maximum dollar amount is less than 
the AFP pump limit, the approved maximum dollar amount takes precedence.  
Note: When this occurs in either the ATL101 or higher message formats, the BUYPASS host 
sends a Response Code value of F (the Partial Authorization code for either the ATL101 
or higher message format).  There is no special indicator in the ATL100 or ISO 8583 
message formats when the WEX host returns an approved maximum dollar amount in 
the Authorization Response that is different than the amount sent in the Authorization 
Request. 
For all WEX fleet card in-store transactions, approval/denial is based on the actual amount sent 
in the Authorization Request. 
10.1.11. Product Code Data  
 
The Product Code Data is required for all fleet transactions types.  For Inside Pre-Pay 
Authorization Only, if the product code is known, it can be sent from the POS.  If the product 
code is unknown, the Buypass host will send the default value of ‘074’ according to the Wright 
Express specification. 
10.1.12. Track Support Requirements  
The following track support requirements must be met when processing all electronic WEX fleet 
card transactions:  
• The default track that is sent to BUYPASS on an original transaction should be Track 2. 
• Card data provided in a follow-on transaction should be full Track 2 Data. If full Track 2 Data 
is not available for follow-on transactions, partial Track 2 Data should be used. 
Note: This does not apply to the TransArmor-VeriFone Edition processing when sending full 
Track 2 Data. Partial Track 2 Data consists of the Primary Account Number, followed by “=” 
sign—rather than a field separator—followed by the 4-digit expiration date (Storage format:  
YYMM).  No other discretionary data follows the 4-digit expiration date. 
10.1.13. Available Products 
For all WEX fleet card Automated Fuel P ump (AFP) Authorization Only and Inside Pre -Pay 
Authorization Only, the WEX host requires the Available Products indicator to be sent from the 
POS.  This indicator informs WEX that the POS supports the ability to receive information on the 
available quantity and fuel types allowed.  
WEX will interrogate the 2-digit restriction code and the Available Product indicator in the request 
to determine the products to be allowed.

10.2.1.1. Technology Selection 
The WEX Chip card contains a Technology Indicator located at offset 33 from the beginning of 
Track 2 data. 
When the WEX card is swiped and the Technology Indicator value is equal to 2, the terminal 
must request the cardholder to use the chip. 
See section 10.3, “Card Layout,” for additional information.  
10.2.1.2. Application Selection 
When the WEX chip card has more than one application, WEX recommends the terminal allow 
merchant priority in selecting the application. 
Note: Version 4.1.2 of the WEX specification only supports one AID. 
A WEX chip-enabled terminal must support one of the following methods for application 
selection: 
• When only one application is mutually supported, this application is automatically selected.

10.2.1.4. Application Selection Response Analysis 
In addition to the EMV-defined checks performed on application selection response, the terminal 
must extract the WEX proprietary data element Tag ‘DF30’ (Fuel Card usage bitmap) when it is 
present. 
After the application selection response analysis, the terminal may process in parallel both the 
‘EMV Processing Part 1’ function and the ‘Prompting’ function. 
Note: For additional information on EMV Processing (Part 1), see section 10.2.1.6, “EMV 
Processing (Part 1) Results.”  
 For additional information on prompting function, see section 10.2.1.5, “Prompting.” 
When it is not possible to process both functions in parallel, the terminal must first process the 
EMV Processing (Part 1) function. 
The transaction amount communicated in Tag ‘9F02’ is: 
• Required to be the accurate amount for a purchase transaction 
• Preferred to be an estimated amount for a pre-authorization transaction (alternative is to use 
a fixed holding amount but this is only available with the WEX card) 
10.2.1.5. Prompting 
Chip prompt information is stored in the following tag: 
• Tag ‘DF30’ – Fuel Card usage bitmap 
The prompts are translated using the table in Appendix E, “WEX Chip-Specific POS Prompt 
Codes.” 
Example of a chip requesting driver id and odometer would result in the values: ‘260000’ and 
‘2A0000”. 
The Prompt Code in the Data Element field of Byte 1 and Prompt Part 2 of Byte 3 are fixed.  
The other values (numeric/alphanumeric, mandatory/optional, print and display fields are 
expected to be supported in the WEX Chip release.  The Dependence on Byte 2 and Byte 2 are 
for future support. 
Note: For terminals that cannot support alphabetic or special characters, they will be certified 
by WEX with numeric only response. 
All prompts should be collected by the terminal.  If a terminal cannot request a specific prompt 
(for example, a prompt is not available on the terminal), the prompt is skipped.  Do not send a 
value that is not entered on the terminal.

10.2.1.6. EMV Processing (Part 1) Results Analysis 
The terminal application must analyze the card decision communicated in the response of the 
‘Start ICC transaction response’. 
• Transaction Rejection: 
For either an offline approval (TC) or transaction declined (AAC), the terminal must: 
o Stop prompting information to the Driver (if the function was processed in parallel with 
the chip transaction) 
o Request the Driver to remove the card from the chip reader 
o Inform the Driver the transaction is rejected (the terminal should not allow the Driver to 
swipe the magnetic stripe and repeat the transaction using the magnetic stripe) 
o When Troubleshooting function is supported, store in the terminal the information related 
to the transaction declined 
o Process ‘Transaction Completion’ function 
• Process Online: 
o When the ‘Faster EMV Solution’ function is active in the terminal, the terminal must 
complete the transaction with the card prior to processing of the information available in 
the IFSF API ‘Start ICC transaction response’ other than card decision. 
• The terminal application must use the ISFS API ‘Complete ICC transaction Device 
Request’ and inform the card that the online authorization was completed by a 
communication problem and the transaction must be declined [EMV Authorization 
Response Code = “Z3” – Unable to Go Online, offline declined] 
• The API response must be ignored 
• The terminal application must request the Driver to remove the card from the chip 
reader and must inform that the transaction is in process. 
o The remaining part of the function is independent of the activation or not of the ‘Quick 
Chip Solution’ function. 
• Prompt the Driver for the information requested in data element Tag ‘DF30’ : Fuel 
Card usage bitmap when not already prompted during the “application selection 
response analysis” function 
• If the WEX proprietary data element (Tag ‘DF31’ : Fuel Card usage bitmap 
(Complementary values)) is not empty [all bytes set to ‘00’], prompt the Driver for the 
information requested in this data  
▪ If the Terminal has been developed to support the following tags, it will run the 
additional function linked to the presence of the following proprietary data 
elements: 
• Tag ‘DF37’ : 3rd Party Reference Data Generation 2 
• Tag ‘DF38’ : Loyalty ID 
• Tag ‘DF36’ : Relationship Codes 
▪ Continue with the online authorization process

10.2.1.7. Online Authorization Process 
When the transaction is successfully processed online, the terminal must apply the following 
decisions: 
• When the chip card is not present when the response is received and 
o The terminal is in Faster EMV mode, the terminal must apply WEX Authorization Host 
decision. 
o The terminal is NOT in Faster EMV mode, the transaction is aborted. 
• When the chip card is present and the response is received, the terminal must apply WEX 
Chip Application decision that may confirm WEX Authorization Host decision. 
• When the transaction is able to go online for authorization, it is possible that host based 
prompts may be returned. 
• When DE 55 is present in the online response message and data element Issuer 
Authentication Data (tag ‘91’) is part of the chip data, the terminal must be capable to extract 
the 8 least bytes of Issuer Authentication Data.  The usage of these 8 bytes (called 
‘Proprietary Authentication Data’). 
• When the transaction does not get a response from WEX (communication error) 
o If the chip is still present the terminal may approve the transaction offline using the chip 
values.  (The message reason code must reflect that the chip was used.)  See 10.2.3.4, 
“Offline Purchase Restrictions.” 
o Alternatively, the merchant may call for authorization.  (The message reason code must 
reflect that the VRU was used to authorization the transaction.) 
10.2.1.8. Usage of ‘Proprietary Authentication Data’ 
Currently, there is no usage defined for the 8 least significant bytes of Issuer Authentication 
Data (called Proprietary Authentication Data). The terminal must ignore their values. 
10.2.1.9. Transaction Completion 
• Transaction Declined: A receipt may be printed. 
• Preauthorization transaction approved: 
o By WEX, the POS terminal must follow all limits returned. 
o By VRU, the POS terminal must not allow the transaction to exceed the amount 
authorized.  The completion will be sent up as soon as communication is restored. (The 
message reason code will reflect that the transaction was approved after calling the 
VRU.) 
o By the Chip, the POS terminal must follow the limits as outlined in section 10.2.3.5, 
“Offline Purchase Restrictions.”  The completion will be sent up as soon as 
communication is restored. (The message reason code will reflect that the transaction 
was approved by the Chip.) 
• Sales transaction approved: 
o By WEX, the POS terminal will complete its local processing.

10.2.1.10. Card Removal 
When the card is removed from the chip reader before a ‘card removal request’ from the 
terminal, the transaction must be aborted.  The terminal must inform the Driver that the 
transaction is aborted. 
If the terminal has already received an authorization response from the WEX Authorization 
Host, the terminal must send a reversal message to the WEX Authorization Host. 
The terminal may print a receipt. 
10.2.1.11. Troubleshooting 
In case of abnormal transaction rejection, the terminal should store information related to the 
declined transaction for facilitating potential troubleshooting investigation. 
• Transaction declined by the WEX Chip Application without attempt to process the 
transaction online 
• Transaction declined by the WEX Chip Application after an authorization delivered by WEX 
Online Authorization Host 
The recommended minimum information to store in the terminal related to the last transaction is: 
• Chip-related data elements normally present in the authorization request message (even if 
no message sent) 
• Some data elements read in the chip during the EMV transaction (Issuer Action Code (IAC) 
parameters, truncated value of the PAN and PAN Sequence Number value) 
The terminal should support a maintenance function allowing to print or to display the 
information stored. 
It should also be possible to print or display at least the following terminal parameters involved 
in the decision process: 
• Current Terminal Action Code (TAC) parameters  
• Current Terminal Capabilities parameter 
• Current Additional Terminal Capabilities parameter 
10.2.1.12. Exception Processing 
The following exception processing should occur, if the transaction is cancelled during its 
processing: 
• Before the 1st GENERATE AC command, the card may be simply powered off.

10.2.2.4. Cardholder Verification Method 
WEX Chip cards are accepted at both Unattended and Attended terminals: 
Unattended terminals: 
• Support of ‘No CVM Required’ is mandatory 
• Support of online enciphered PIN is optional 
• Support of offline PIN is optional 
• Support of signature is not allowed 
Attended terminals: 
• Support of ‘No CVM Required’ is optional 
• Support of online enciphered PIN is optional 
• Support of offline PIN is optional 
• Support of signature is mandatory 
10.2.2.5. Offline Card Authentication Methods 
WEX requirements related to the support of offline Card Authentication Methods (CAM) are: 
• An offline capable terminal must support both DDA and CDA (SDA is optional) 
• An online-only terminal may support no offline CAM 
• When CDA is supported, CDA must be implemented according to EMV 4.2 or later versions.  
The terminal must use the CDA EMV-defined Mode n°1 defined in EMV 4.3 - Book 2 that 
consists in: 
o Request CDA on 1st GENERATE AC command on ARQC, and 
o Request CDA on 2nd GENERATE AC on TC after approved online authorization. 
• When CDA is supported, the terminal should verify before Terminal Action Analysis that it 
contains the Certification Authority Public Key identified by the card.  Terminals that can 
perform RSA certificate verification quickly are recommended to retrieve the Issuer public 
key and ICC public key prior Terminal Action Analysis. 
• When offline CAM is supported, the terminal must be capable to support at least two WEX 
Certification Authority Public Keys for the WEX RID.  (EMV mandates to support at least 6 
Certification Authority Public Keys per RID) 
• When offline CAM is supported, the terminal must be capable to support RSA key length of 
248 bytes and RSA key exponent equal to either 3 or (216 + 1) 
• The terminal must be capable to check the integrity of the Certification Authority Public 
Keys.

10.2.3.3. Online Purchase Restrictions and Validation 
WEX’s preference is for online authorization. 
The POS only uses the purchase restrictions on the magnetic stripe or chip if the merchant 
location is offline to WEX and cannot receive an authorization.  
10.2.3.4. POS Receipts 
The fleet card receipt requirements listed in section 4, ‘Receipt Requirements’ apply to WEX 
Chip transactions. 
In addition, WEX Chip transactions must also include the following items on all approved fleet 
card receipts: 
• AID of application selected 
• Application Preferred Name (recommended) or Application Label of the application selected 
• Cryptogram generated by the card and communicated to the terminal in the 1st GENERATE 
AC command response 
Notes:  
• The receipt printing requirement for WEX Chip cards is included in Tag ‘DF30.’ 
• The field “Sequence Number” printed on the receipt for WEX transactions represents the 
WEX Invoice Number. 
10.2.3.5. Offline Processing 
The POS device is permitted to support offline processing for WEX Chip cards in the following 
manner: 
• Chip limits 
• Call for authorization 
If connectivity is lost while processing a Chip transaction: 
• The POS has already collected the chip based prompt and may proceed to use the Chip 
Limits for the purchase amount.  Alternatively, a call for authorization may be used for the 
purchase amount. 
• The POS will process production validations/restrictions based on the chip. 
• The POS will limit the fuel purchased to the fuel amount and the non-fuel purchase to the 
non-fuel amount.  If the POS does not process these amounts, the transaction should call 
for authorization and be limited to fuel products only. 
10.2.3.6. Offline Purchase Restrictions 
In a standard EMV solution, if the terminal supports authorization using the chip, the POS will

11.1.4. Manual Entry – Track Data 
Manual entry is allowed for COMDATA cards. (see COMDATA Express Code Processing and 
COMDATA Check Processing sections for those rules). 
Track 2 data should be present on the card and that is the account data that should be 
submitted on swiped or chip read transactions. 
Track 1 data will not be accepted. 
 
11.1.5. Purchase Restriction 
In online processing, limits for each allowed fuel type for the card will be returned in the 
authorization response. The terminal is expected to send a list of fuel products that are available 
to the cardholder in the Authorization Only request transaction.  Comdata will send limits for 
each in the Authorization Only response.  Fuel products not listed in the response will be 
considered off limit by the terminal.  Comdata will return two other category limits to the 
terminal:   
• A Cash Available limit, which will be sent to the Terminal as product code “955”. 
• A Non-Fuel Product limit, which will be sent to the Terminal as product code “000”. 
Any Non-fuel products data, including amount, will be sent as part of the Capture request.  
COMDATA may decline a transaction that includes a Non-fuel product whose amount exceeds 
a limit for its category. 
Offline processing is not supported. 
 
11.1.6. Authorization Amount  
For all COMDATA fleet card automated fuel pump (AFP) transactions, the host returns an 
approved maximum dollar amount in the Authorization Response that is used to authorize the 
pump. This amount may differ from the amount in the original Authorization Request transmitted 
by the device. If the approved maximum dollar amount is more than the AFP pump limit, the 
pump limit may take precedence. If the approved maximum dollar amount is less than the AFP 
pump limit, the approved maximum dollar amount takes precedence.  
In addition, the authorization response may contain amount limits on fuel products. It is the 
responsibility of the POS device to enforce these limits. Format of limits is contained in the 
applicable message format specification.

11.1.7. Product Data  
In addition to the Product Code Data that must be sent in all fleet transactions, COMDATA Fleet 
transactions have the following rules: 
• In an authorization request, all fuel products available for dispensing at the pump should 
be sent in the Product Code Data segment with the unit price, a product quantity of 1, 
and an appropriate total amount (unit price multiplied by quantity). 
• In an authorization response, the limits for all these fuels will be returned. 
• In a capture request, the actual amounts for each product should be sent in the Product 
Code Data segment, as well as product codes, unit price, quantity and actual amount for 
any fuel and non-fuel products included in the purchase. 
 
11.1.8. Additional Data  
The terminal will need to support Universal Unique ID (UUID) in requests and responses.  This 
support includes: 
• Sending a flag in requests that indicates it can accept a UUID in the response (see 
applicable message format specification),  
• Receiving and capturing the UUID in the response (see applicable message format 
specification) 
• Sending the UUID from an original transaction on any subsequent transactions (see 
applicable message format specification).  For example: 
o Account Verify (receives UUID1) → Authorization (sends UUID1) → Completion (sends UUID 1) 
o Account Verify (receives UUID2) → Sale (sends UUID2)  → Void of Sale (sends UUID2) 
In addition to the prompt and product data, the device should be prepared to send and receive 
any additional data described in the Enhanced Fleet data section of the applicable message 
specification.  
AFP devices should always send Completions, and not Purchases.

15. WEX OTR Fleet Card Processing  
This chapter discusses the following topics related to WEX OTR fleet card processing:  
• Processing requirements  
 
15.2. Processing Requirements  
This section discusses the following processing requirements:  
• Supported transactions  
• Terminal Special/Prompt Codes  
• POS Prompt Codes  
• Manual entry  
• Purchase Restriction  
• Authorization Amount  
• Product Data  
• Additional Data 
 
15.2.1. Supported Transactions  
The following transactions are supported for the WEX OTR fleet cards:  
• POS Capture Transaction  
• POS Authorization Only Transaction  
• CAT Capture Transaction  
• CAT Authorization Only Transaction  
• POS Return/Refund Transaction  
• POS Reversal/Void Transaction  
 
Note:  
Store and Forward: When either the device loses connection to BUYPASS, or BUYPASS 
loses connection to the WEX OTR Card authorizer, the device will take responsibility for storing 
the transactions. When the connection is restored, the transactions will be forwarded as 
captures without prior authorization to the appropriate acquiring host. 
 
15.2.2. Terminal Special/Prompt Codes  
In order for BUYPASS to receive WEX OTR fleet card transactions, the Merchant Profile at 
BUYPASS must have Terminal Special Code 179 enabled. If the terminal is to accept only 
NGFC cards, it should be configured with Terminal Special Code 180 instead. 
 
The POS application must be able to read the Card Type codes 091 and 092 sent in the Table 
Load response. In the case where an application does not process a Table Load from 
BUYPASS, the application must provide a method to determine whether WEX OTR fleet cards 
are allowed.

15.2.3. POS Prompt Codes  
The POS or CAT device must interpret the authorization response to determine what prompts to 
request from the customer.  
• If the authorization is approved, the POS must verify the validity of these prompts based 
on the prompt formatting data returned in the authorization response before authorizing 
the pump to operate.  
• If the authorization is declined with code “DX”, the authorizer is indicating that additional 
information in the form of prompts is required before the pump is authorized. The device 
must request the prompts indicated in the authorization response and include them in 
another authorization request. This process may be repeated up to 3 times. Each 
iteration from the POS should include all available prompt responses, even if they were 
previously accepted. If, at that time, the authorizer is still not satisfied, the POS must 
decline the transaction. Once an authorization approval is received, the pump may be 
authorized to operate. 
• If an authorization is declined with code “D7”, the authorizer is indicating that one or 
more received prompts do not match expected values. In this case, the invalid prompts 
will be indicated by a “?” in the prompt formatting section. If desired, these transactions 
can be retried after re-prompting for the incorrect value. Remember that all available 
prompts including those that were not marked as incorrect should be sent up with the 
retry. 
In either case, when pumping is complete, the values entered for all prompts must be sent with 
the capture message. Refer to the WEX OTR Request and Response data in the applicable 
message specification for formatting details. 
 
15.2.4. Manual Entry  
Manual entry is not allowed for any WEX OTR card. 
 
15.2.5. Purchase Restriction 
In online processing, limits for each allowed product category for the card will be returned in the 
authorization response. Any product category not included in the authorization response is 
considered not allowed. In offline processing mode, the device must make the determination 
about what products are allowed for offline purchase based on settings in the Dynamic Card 
Table. 
 
15.2.6. Authorization Amount  
For all WEX OTR fleet card automated fuel pump (AFP) transactions, the host returns an 
approved maximum dollar amount in the Authorization Response that, along with the prompts 
also return in the authorization response, is used to authorize the pump. This amount may differ 
from the amount in the original Authorization Request transmitted by the device. If the approved 
maximum dollar amount is more than the AFP pump limit, the pump limit may take precedence. 
If the approved maximum dollar amount is less than the AFP pump limit, the approved 
maximum dollar amount takes precedence.

In addition, the authorization response may contain quantity or amount limits on fuel and non-
fuel products. It is the responsibility of the POS device to enforce these limits. Format of limits is 
contained in the applicable message format specification. 
Note: When this occurs in either the ATL101 or higher message formats, the BUYPASS host 
sends a Response Code value of F (the Partial Authorization code for either the ATL101 or 
higher message format). There is no special indicator in the ATL100 or ISO 8583 message 
formats when the host returns an approved maximum dollar amount in the Authorization 
Response that is different than the amount sent in the Authorization Request. 
 
15.2.7. Product Data  
In addition to the Product Code Data that must be sent in all fleet transactions, WEX OTR Fleet 
transactions have the following rules: 
• In an authorization request, all fuel products available for dispensing at the pump should 
be sent in the Product Code Data segment with the unit price, a product quantity of 1, 
and an appropriate total amount. 
• In an authorization response, the limits for all of these fuel products as well as the limits 
for all non-fuel product categories allowed for this card will be returned. 
• In a capture request, the actual amounts for each product should be sent in the Product 
Code Data segment, and the total amount for each product category included in the 
purchase should be sent in the non-fuel product portion of the WEX OTR data. Product 
categories are included in the Product portion of the Dynamic Card Table. 
• If the customer does not use Dynamic Card Table, the mapping of the product code to 
the product category contained in Appendix M can be used. 
 
15.2.8. Additional Data  
In addition to the prompt and product data, the device should be prepared to send and receive 
any additional data described in the WEX OTR data section of the applicable message 
specification.

This section discusses the following processing requirements:

• POS Authorization Only Transaction 
Note:  
Store and Forward: Not applicable to Money Code. 
 
16.1.2. Terminal Special/Prompt Codes  
In order for BUYPASS to process Money Code transactions, the Merchant Profile at BUYPASS 
must have Terminal Special Code 179 enabled.  
The POS application must be able to read the Card Type code 093 sent in the Table Load 
response. In the case where an application does not process a Table Load from BUYPASS, the 
application must provide a method to determine whether Money Code transactions are allowed.  
 
16.1.3. POS Prompt Codes  
No prompt data will be exchanged for Money Code transactions. 
 
16.1.4. Manual Entry  
All Money Code transactions are entered manually. The code value entered should be sent in 
the account number field and the expiration date should be skipped.

16.1.5. Purchase Restriction 
It is up to the device to allow or disallow any products for Money Code transactions. No product 
validation will be done at the host, but product data should be sent and will be collected as usual 
for a WEX OTR transaction. See the applicable message specification for formatting details. 
 
16.1.6. Authorization Amount  
In all cases, the Money Code transaction will be approved for the full amount or declined. There 
is no partial authorization for Money Code transactions.

transactions have the following rules:

the purchase should be sent in the non-fuel product portion of the WEX OTR data. 
Product categories are included in the Product portion of the Dynamic Card Table.

In addition to the Product data, the following elements may be included in the WEX OTR Data 
for Money Code transactions: 
 
• Customer last name and first initial (Optional) 
• Check Number (Mandatory) 
 
See the applicable message specification for details on how this data should be formatted in the 
WEX OTR Data.
